rationale: Atlantica is a genuine infrastructure owner/operator and ECP and Temasek remain current investors after the December 12, 2024 take-private. It nevertheless fails the census geography rule at manager-level company scope: Atlantica is headquartered in London, describes itself as operating across North America, Europe and South America, and continues material operating and development activity in each region. North America represented 61% of operating power capacity in the September 2025 presentation, but that majority asset share does not make the global platform primarily based in or dedicated to the United States, Canada or Mexico.
recommendedChanges: Exclude Atlantica's global manager-level platform from the North American direct infrastructure-equity PortCo census.
Preserve the May 27, 2024 announcement, December 10 court sanction and December 12 legal close as historical acquisition research.
Record ECP and Temasek as current investors only in the preserved exclusion history; do not infer a named ECP fund, Temasek vehicle or ownership percentage.
Do not split Atlantica's U.S., Canadian or Mexican projects and subsidiaries into separate PortCos unless a manager separately presents and owns one as a standalone investment.
Treat the queued plc name as the historical acquired-company identity and resolve current group/opco legal names only if a later scorecard or deal record requires them.
unresolvedQuestions: The complete institutional co-investor list and investor-level percentages are not publicly disclosed.
The ECP fund and Temasek acquisition vehicle are not publicly disclosed.
Post-take-private group and operating-company legal names differ across current materials.
